args.rationale: Inpatient with MRSA bacteremia who deteriorated quickly into cardiogenic shock (physical_exam_005). He also has DIC (lab_007). Echocardiography showed new LV wall-motion abnormalities and a pericardial effusion that progressed to tamponade (ecg_008). Emergency pericardiocentesis drained yellowish, turbid fluid (procedure_result_011), which suggests purulent pericarditis. He needs ICU-level hemodynamic support, correction of the DIC, and emergent definitive surgical drainage. Pericardial fluid analysis, pericardial culture, TEE, CT and angiography results were not available in the source, so the diagnosis is still uncertain.
args.followup_or_handoff: Hand off to the ICU team and to cardiothoracic surgery for the emergent surgical pericardial drainage already ordered (pericardial window or pericardiotomy), with exploration for a myocardial or perivalvular abscess. Handoff items: (1) Vasopressor and inotrope support, with invasive arterial and central venous monitoring. Avoid volume depletion until the tamponade is fully relieved. Monitor the pericardial drain output for reaccumulation. (2) Treat the DIC with blood products guided by coagulation labs and platelet count. Type and crossmatch now. (3) Continue vancomycin: a 25 mg/kg IV loading dose was ordered, then pharmacist AUC-guided dosing (target AUC/MIC 400-600) adjusted to renal function. The current antibiotic regimen and allergies were not reported and must be confirmed. Consider switching to daptomycin 8-10 mg/kg IV every 24 hours if bacteremia persists, vancomycin MIC is ≥1.5, or he has an allergy. (4) Send pericardial fluid and tissue for Gram stain, culture, cell count, glucose, protein and LDH. Draw repeat blood cultures every 24-48 hours until they clear. (5) Get a TEE once stable to look for endocarditis or abscess. Cardiology will decide on coronary angiography for the new wall-motion abnormalities, weighed against the bleeding risk from DIC. (6) Request an infectious diseases consult. Plan at least 4-6 weeks of antibiotics from the first negative blood culture.
